raw_response:
*settling into the role of the farmer — speaking in her voice now*

---

Aiya, it's that time of year again. My back isn't what it was, but the land still needs working. Let me think about how this year will go.

I've been farming this patch for more years than I can count, and my mother-in-law farmed it before me. Eleven mu and some — it's not much, but between me, my husband, and our boy (when he's home from the city), we get by. The well still pumps, the wheat still grows, that's what matters.

**The wheat that's already in the ground** — I planted it back in October like always, right after the Double Ninth Festival 重阳 more or less. I used the same seed as last year, the 济麦 kind that old Wang down the road swears by. Already spread one bag of 复合肥 per mu when I plowed it in — that's the 15-15-15 kind, 40 kg bags, costs about 150 块 a bag now, more than last year. Everything costs more.

Come spring — should be starting soon, maybe in a couple weeks when the ground warms — I'll walk the field and see how it looks. If the wheat's come up yellow or thin, I'll put down urea 尿素, about half a bag per mu, maybe 12-15 jin. If it looks fine, I put a little less. My neighbor's daughter-in-law went to that agriculture school and she says we old people put down too much, but I say: better a little extra than watch it fail. I've seen bad years.

Irrigation — I'll water it three times like always. Once before winter freeze — already done, that 冻水 is important. Then once at 返青 when it's coming back green, and one more when it's filling out the heads. If there's good rain, maybe I skip one to save on the electric pump. Pumping isn't free anymore, the card runs down fast.

For weeds, I'll spray once in spring. Herbicide 除草剂, the one for wheat fields. My son-in-law buys it for me from the co-op, about 20 块 a mu. I don't mess with bug sprays much for wheat — usually no need.

Harvest in June. I hire the 联合收割机 like everyone does — about 50 块 a mu, done in half a day. Can't be cutting by hand at my age, and besides nobody does that anymore.

**Then comes maize** — this is the hard part. The week after wheat harvest, I have to clear the straw and get maize in the ground right away. No time to plow proper — we do 免耕 these days, just use the no-till planter, neighbor's son has one, he does ours for 40 块 a mu. Saves time.

I plant the same maize seed my husband's cousin sells — 郑单958 or whatever hybrid he has that year. Costs me 40-some 块 a mu for seed. I put down a bit of fertilizer with the planting, maybe 30 kg of compound per mu since the soil still has some strength from the wheat fertilizer. Then when the maize is knee-high, I side-dress urea — half a bag per mu.

Maize doesn't need as much water in summer if the rains come. Sometimes I water once at tasseling 抽雄 if it's dry, otherwise the sky does the work. 

Pests — I spray once for 玉米螟 corn borer usually, and herbicide after planting. That's it.

Harvest in late September, before the autumn rain comes. Hire the combine again.

**What I'm worried about this year:** Fertilizer is dear, electricity for the well is dear. My savings are thin. If the maize price is low at harvest like last year, this whole year might just break even. But what else can I do? The land must be planted. I can't leave it fallow — the village would talk, and anyway we need the grain for ourselves plus some to sell.

I'll plant what I always plant. I'll do what I always do. Saints and gods willing, it'll be a normal year.
